Commentary.Commentary: Nothing to show for the away side. Subashis Roy was the pick of the bowlers taking 3 for 118 but the wickets didn't quite come in time for his side. Rahim lacked imagination as he failed to motivate his players, admittedly. They know what they are up against. The home side has the bowling attack to trouble them. They will be itching to go at the visitors. Join us in a while for the reply from the Tigers.

South Africa have declared! A superb batting performance from them after being asked to bat. Their openers laid the platform with a 243-run stand. Both Elgar and Markram scored tons to set it up. Amla and du Plessis then stitched a 247-run stand to take their side past 500. Both of them helped themselves with a ton each. It is a mammoth score on this wicket which is starting to misbehave a tad.
Stays back to this one and tucks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Around off, driven with the spin to sweeper cover for a run.
Quinton shapes for the big hit but the bowler bowls it outside off. He resists and block it.
Fraction short outside off, de Kock backs away to cut it but ends up chopping it to point.
Floated outside off, eased to covers.
Shorter in length on middle, pushed off the back foot to mid on.
Mahmudullah to roll his arm over now.
Bouncer outside off, slow in pace. Takes ages to come to de Kock who pulls it to square leg for a run.
The off-cutter from Fizz again which he bowls with great control. Faf backs away and places it to covers for a run.
Full length delivery on middle, Quinton knocks it to long on to rotate strike.
Short delivery at a slower pace in line of the stumps, de Kock is early into his pull shot and misses it.
Off-cutter on middle and leg, du Plessis makes room and strokes it to mid off for a brisk single.
Yorker on off, Faf can do nothing about it apart from keeping it out.

Mustafizur Rahman returns for a bowl. The South African players are putting their whites on. Might have a declaration soon? 565/4 - This is the highest team score in Bloemfontein. Previous highest was 563 all out by SA vs IND, 2001.
Bouncer on off, de Kock drops his wrists to leave it alone.
Well bowled! De Kock makes room and Roy rolls his fingers on this one. He looks to ramp it over the keeper but misses.
Fullish on middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a run.
De Kock advances down the track and Roy bowls it shortish on middle and leg. Pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Short delivery on middle and leg, Quinton thinks about a pull but bails out of it.
Very full delivery attacking the stumps, de Kock jams it out off the inner half through backward square leg. A couple taken.
FOUR! Great stroke! Tossed up around off, du Plessis goes inside out over extra cover for a majestic boundary. 21 from the over.
Turns this one with the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
SIX! What a hit! Quinton at his free flowing best! Fullish on off, de Kock clears his front leg and heaves it over cow corner for a biggie. He is having fun out there.
Goes for the fancy reverse sweep but gets hit high on the pads. A stifled appeal for an LBW follows but that was probably spinning down leg.
FOUR! Well played! Floated outside off, de Kock makes good use of his feet and lifts it over mid off to find the fence.

SIX! Boom! Slow through the air on off, de Kock crouches and brings out the slog sweep. Has executed it to perfection and the ball clears the deep mid-wicket fence with ease. It takes some time to locate the ball. Finally it has been found.
Fullish ball on middle, Quinton clips it to wide mid on for a run.
Dug in short around leg stump, de Kock ducks under it.
Driven towards the mid off region.
Fuller in length, eased to mid off.

Ouch! That must hurt! Short of a length around off, angling in. Du Plessis looks to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto his box. The batsmen sneak in a run. The skipper is in pain. It is surely not a good feeling.
Back of a length outside off, punched crisply to covers.
Risky! Stays back to this one and looks to cut it but is cramped for room. Somehow manages to keep it out.

Not Out! That was a clear bump ball. Tossed up around off, de Kock brings out the reverse sweep. He hasn't executed it well and the ball flies towards Kayes at first slip. He anticipates it well and takes it nicely. He is claiming the catch but the umpires are not sure. It is referred upstairs. The soft signal is not out. The replays show that Quinton had hit it straight onto the ground.
Is that out? Imrul Kayes is claiming a catch off de Kock at first slip. Looks close. The soft signal is not out.
FOUR! Shot! Fullish delivery around off, de Kock kneels and slog sweeps it hard past the backward square leg fielder for a boundary.
Slow through the air outside off, de Kock is a bit early into his drive. Gets it uppishly towards mid off but safe.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Floated outside off, eased to long off for a run.
Quinton de Kock strides out to bat.

OUT! Timber! A majestic knock from the mighty Hash comes to an end! Tame dismissal really. Amla walks across a long way across his stumps, trying to force the issue. Roy spots him and smartly bowls a length delivery in line of the stumps. Hashim misses and sees the furniture behind him get shattered. Third wicket for the pacer. The mammoth 247-run stand finally comes to an end. Some relief for Bangladesh!
On a length on leg stump, tucked with soft hands to mid on for a run.
FOUR! Textbook cover drive! Fullish delivery outside off, du Plessis takes a reasonable stride forward and creams it through extra cover to find the fence. All timing and grace!
Overpitched on off, Faf clears his front leg and times it crisply but finds the mid on fielder again.
Similar length ball, straight this time. Du Plessis strokes it to mid on.
Starts off with a fuller length delivery well outside off, holding its line. Faf plants his front foot across to allow it through.

No declaration then, the two South African batsmen want some more runs. It is bright and sunny at the moment in Bloemfontein. Wonderful conditions to play cricket. Hashim Amla and Faf du Plessis stride out to continue batting. Subashis Roy to bowl first up after lunch. A slip and gully in place. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

The scoring rate for the Proteas tells you how badly the away side has bowled. Are these runs enough for du Plessis to declare? Let's see if they continue to bat or have a go at the Tigers. Conditions are still good for batting but pressure is a funny little factor. Stay tuned for all the action. Join us in a while for the second session.

South Africa continue to dominate! It has been a batting masterclass from the experienced duo of Hashim Amla and Faf du Plessis, who have sailed past their centuries nonchalantly. Intent has been missing on the part of the tourists and so has been the discipline. Too many hit-me balls from them and the hosts have obliged by putting them away.
Shorter in length outside off, hit through the diving mid off fielder for a single. That's Lunch, Day 2!
Last ball before Lunch...
Shortish outside off, punched to long off for a single.
Lands it around middle, Amla defends it from his crease.
Flatter outside off, pushed towards point by the batsman for a single.
Comes right forward and defends it watchfully towards mid off.
Fuller on middle, driven towards covers.

FOUR! Hello, says the pitch. Where did that come from? Good length outside off, bounces a lot more, Amla fends at it and gets an outside edge. The ball flies wide of the keeper for a boundary. The SA bowlers won't mind watching this, though.
Around off on a length, Amla keeps it out watchfully.
Turns one towards mid-wicket from his crease.
Good length outside off, left alone again.
Outside off on a length, left alone.
FOUR! All class! Good length outside off, Amla opens the face of the bat and gets it through backward point for a boundary. Hundred for Roy as well.
Subashis Roy to have a bowl now.
Shorter outside off, punched to covers who does not misfield this time around.
On the pads again, worked through square leg for a single.
Flatter around leg, turned through mid-wicket for a single.
Amla gets across and punches it to long on for a run.
Turns it through wide mid on for a single.
Shorter outside off, punched to covers. The fielder fumbles and allows a couple of runs.
Mahmudullah called on for a bowl. Even Bangladesh want SA to declare early.
Amla lunges forward and turns it towards the leg side.
Drives it towards mid off from his crease.
Lands it outside off,  slammed to long off for a single.
Turns it through backward square leg for a couple of runs. Good running gets them the third.
Fuller outside off, pushed to long off for a single.
Fuller around off, Amla punches it through mid off for a single.
FOUR! Pristine! Fuller and outside off, du Plessis reads it well and creams it through wide of mid off for a boundary.
Shorter in length and on the body, tucked to long leg for a run.
Fuller on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Good length around middle, punched towards covers from his crease.
Woah! Amla walks a long way across even before Rahman bowls one, flicks it through backward square leg for a single.
Good length around leg, worked through backward square leg for a single. 500 up for SA!
Shorter outside off, punched to covers.
Fuller around off, driven through mid off for another single.
Flatter around off, hit back to the bowler by du Plessis.
Dances down the wicket and pushes one towards cover-point.
Batting masterclass! This is only the second time that South Africa have had four centurions in an innings in Test cricket.
Drives it through mid off for a run.
Fuller outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Bouncer! Bumper by Rahman, Amla ducks under it.
Slants it around off, du Plessis taps it towards covers and takes a single.
Length ball outside off, hit towards covers.

FOUR! Captain leading from the front! Ton for du Plessis! Fuller around middle, turned through mid-wicket for a boundary. That is a hundred for Faf du Plessis. This is his 7th Test ton, his first of 2017, his 5th in South Africa, his first against Bangladesh and his 3rd as skipper. Looks like SA will bat on for now. Also, Faf's ton is the 50th by a Test captain in South Africa.
Too full around off, jammed towards backward point.
Bowls a full toss, du Plessis misses out on it and just pats it back down the wicket.
Time for the Fizz. Can he stop Faf du Plessis from getting the ton? Most of the fielders are inside the 30-yard circle to stop the all-important single.
Shorter outside off, du Plessis punches it towards mid off and takes a quick single. He is now on 99!
Gets a single with a push through mid off.
Flatter outside off, Amla chops it towards point from his crease.
Amla lunges forward and turns it towards mid-wicket.
Shorter around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Loops it around off and middle, du Plessis punches it in the air towards short cover.
Fuller and outside off, guided towards point by Amla.

FOUR! Class! Shorter in length outside off, this time Amla waits, waits and then places it between backward point and short third man for a boundary. Superb shot. The stand is now worth 200! Oh Rahim, what have you done?
Punches this length ball to mid on from his crease.
Intent! Shorter in length outside off, Amla looks to ramp it over the head of the keeper but misses. There is no third man in place so the shot was on indeed.
Shortish outside off, Amla punches it through covers for a couple of runs.
Good length outside off, punched to covers by Amla.
Pushed to short extra cover by Faf du Plessis.
Floats it around off, du Plessis aims to defend but gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
Amla drives one through mid off for a single.
Fuller outside off, Amla comes forward and drives it to mid off.
Fuller in length, Amla swings it towards mid on out of nowhere. Not sure what made Amla play this heave. Signs of declaration around?
Fuller on middle, driven through mid off for a single.
Shorter in length outside off, left alone by Amla.
Shorter in length but on the body, pulled to long leg for a single.
FOUR! Smashed! Shorter in length outside off, du Plessis gets on top of it and pulls it wide of mid on for a boundary.
Shorter in length outside off, du Plessis ducks under it.
Shorter outside off, punched to covers.

Good length outside off, du Plessis punches it to point and Amla takes off. The skipper sends his partner back in time as Mominul scores a direct hit at the bowler's end from covers. No harm done though as Hashim had got back in.
Fuller outside off, driven through covers for a single. Moves on to 91!
Floats it around off, du Plessis punches it towards covers. This time Amla wants a single but is sent back.
Amla guides one through covers for a single.
Amla taps one towards point and Faf wants a single. Sent back in time by Hashim.
Fuller around off, driven through mid off for a single.
Drops it short on middle, punched to long off for a single.
Time for some spin, Taijul Islam to bowl.
FOUR! Century for Rubel! Shorter in length, Faf du Plessis picks it early and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. No doubts, this time around.
Amla punches one towards mid off and takes a single.
Shorter in length outside off, left alone.
Faf du Plessis is advancing towards the sawdust. He is not pleased. It was a glorious stroke which deserved a boundary. He has a wry smile on his face.

What is happening? Fuller in length around off, du Plessis just punches it straight down the ground and assumes that it is a boundary. The ball hits the sawdust sprayed on the way, near the fence and hence slows down. The fielder at long off is slow and not aware of the situation as both du Plessis and Amla were celebrating the boundary which never was, in the middle of the wicket. The throw too was a wild one and it allows Faf to cross over. At the end, only a run taken. Would have been some way to get out that.
Shorter in length outside off, hit off the back foot through covers for a couple of runs.
Good length outside off, punched towards covers by du Plessis.
Fuller in length around off, Amla defends it watchfully.
Good length around off, turned towards the fielder who just came in. The fielder is slow and it allows du Plessis to take the single.
Square leg in place now.
Full again, du Plessis drives it back down the wicket. The bowler stops it in his followthrough.
Full and outside off, a happy leave by du Plessis.
Length ball around off, punched towards mid off by Faf.
Full in length outside off, du Plessis watches it go through safely.
Full and outside off, Hashim is not interested.
Shorter in length outside off, no shot offered by Amla.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Fuller on middle, turned through mid-wicket. Rahim thinks to dive but does not and hence concedes a couple of runs.
Tucks one through the backward square leg region for a single. He moves to 81, could see him declaring once he gets to his ton.
Good length around off, punched towards mid on by the batsman.
Rubel Hossain comes on for a bowl.
Pitched up outside off, another leave by Hashim.
Wow! It is the 19th time SA have had three centurions in a Test innings. If Faf du Plessis scores a century today, it will only be the second time SA will have four centurions.
Fuller outside off, left alone by Amla.
Length ball around off, Amla defends it from his crease.
A tad short around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Good length outside off, left alone by du Plessis.
Faf pulls out at the last moment as he was not ready. The bowler has to head back to his mark.
Good length around off, keeps a tad low, du Plessis turns it towards mid-wicket from his crease.
Goes round the wicket and bowls it outside off on a length, Amla shoulders his arms to it.
Bumper wasted wide outside off, Amla is not even bothered.
Similar ball, similar shot, similar result.
Slants across a length ball, no interest in it by Amla.

FOUR! Hashim, Hashim! Fuller and outside off, Amla just checks his shot coming forward. Gets it in the gap at point and the ball runs away to the fence. A century for Hashim Amla, he has made it look really easy. He raises his bat to acknowledge the applause from the crowd and his teammates. He is now second to only the great Jacques Kallis in terms of Test tons for SA.
Shorter in length, way outside off, Amla lets it go through.
Good length outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Good length outside off, punched to deep point for a single.
Shorter in length outside off, pulled through square leg for a single.
Fuller outside off, du Plessis is not bothered about it.
FOUR! Poor bowling, punished! Nothing ball, on a length outside off, asking to be hit, du Plessis obliges and punches it through covers for a boundary. 450 up for SA!
Milestone Alert - Hashim Amla has gone past the legendary Vivian Richards in terms of runs scored in Tests. One of the best batsmen in the world just keeps on breaking the records.
Good length outside off, left alone by Faf.
Full and wide outside off, Amla is happy to let it go.
Shorter in length outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Fuller and outside off, Faf has his weight back yet gets it through point for a single.
Shorter in length, going across du Plessis who sits and lets it go over him.
Angles it around middle, gets the ball to bounce more, du Plessis takes the bottom hand off the bat and keeps the ball down.
Good length delivery around off, punched towards covers by du Plessis.
Short and wide again, punched in the same region. This time for a couple of runs.
FOUR! In the gap! Shorter in length outside off, Amla waits for it and guides it behind backward point for a boundary. Can't give width to Hashim.
Shorter in length outside off, punched towards gully.
Pitched up around off, Amla comes forward and defends it.
Back of a length outside off, Amla stands tall and punches it towards covers.
Length ball around off, Amla defends it watchfully.
Good length just outside off, Faf defends it watchfully.
Bouncer! Short and wide outside off, left alone by Faf. Too short and hence the umpire signals it a wide.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Good length outside off, du Plessis just stands tall and punches it through covers for a boundary. Also brings up the 150-run stand between the two.
Length ball wide outside off, no problems for du Plessis.
Expect South Africa to declare once both these batsmen get to their tons. Let's see.
Back of a length outside off, Amla guides it to the deep point fielder for a single.
Shorter in length outside off, Amla drops his wrists and lets it go.
Slants one across Amla who watches it sail through to the keeper.
Extra bounce! Good length outside off, bounces a tad more, du Plessis shapes to defend but gets beaten by the extra bounce. Does well to keep it down on the deck though.
Fuller length outside off, du Plessis comes forward and defends it.
Faf gets right behind this length ball and defends it watchfully.
Faf du Plessis comes right forward and defends it.
A lot more closer to the stumps, on a fuller length, Faf is happy to let it go.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Sawdust is being sprayed on the damp areas on the ground. Subashis Roy to bowl from the other end. A slip and a gully in place. A minimum of 83 overs to be bowled today.
Shorter in length outside off, du Plessis slaps it to the cover fielder who fumbles and allows a single.
Did you know? This is the highest 4th wicket partnership for South Africa against Bangladesh in Tests.
Good length around off, punched towards covers.
FOUR! Smashed! Length ball, very wide outside off, Faf du Plessis won't miss out and crashes it through the covers for a boundary.
First runs of the day! Good length outside off, punched off the back foot through point for a couple of runs.
Full and wide outside off, no shot offered by du Plessis.
Slants across a length ball outside off, left alone by Faf.

Time to get the game going. The two South African batsmen Hashim Amla and Faf du Plessis stride out to continue batting. It will be interesting to see how long the hosts bat. Bangladesh begin the day with Mustafizur Rahman. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

Shaun Pollock and Kepler Wessels are doing the pitch report. They say that it was good for strokemaking yesterday. Mention that there will be more pace and bounce today. Add that the South African bowlers will enjoy bowling on this track.
News coming in is that play will begin at 1130 local time, in less than 15 minutes from now. Lunch will be taken at 1300 local time.
1100 local time update - Good news folks! The covers are coming off! We should be starting soon.

1000 local time update - Not a good news guys! We are in for a delayed start. The weather is pretty gloomy and there is light rain around as well. The covers are firmly in place The first thing that is needed is for the drizzle to stop so that the groundsmen can start their work. Let's hope for the best. Stay tuned for more updates.

The tourists have had a lot to think, their captain admitted repeating his mistake of bowling first again but they need to find a way to come back in the game. They will hope to restrict the home side as much as possible and get batting. Let's see how they go about their job. Stay tuned for all the action.

There was a bit of rain around, hope it clears up soon and we get some cricket! On that note, hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the second and final Test between South Africa and Bangladesh in Bloemfontein. Despite losing the toss, the hosts are in a solid position. Their openers laid the platform for them and the middle order will now like to cash in. Could be interesting to see when they declare having already crossed 400.
.... Day 2, Session 1 ....

Elgar fell at the stroke of Tea and two quick wickets post the break might have made the Tigers believe they could turn things around but some poor captaincy and defensive bowling saw the home side get back on top. An unbeaten century stand between du Plessis and Amla has put them in a commanding position. Both will aim to get a big score and bat Bangladesh out of the game if possible. Will they be able to do that or will the visitors stage a comeback? We'll know that tomorrow only. Join us for all the action on Day 2 at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Until then, it's goodbye and take care!

What a day for South Africa! They have amassed over 400 runs in a day and they have the tourists to thank genuinely. Rahim put them into bat and the hosts responded with a 243-run opening stand. Both Elgar and Markram helped themselves with a century each as the Bangladeshi bowlers struggled for any kind of rhythm. They wasted the new ball and the spinner didn't get any purchase from the deck. One wonders what made the captain elect to field on this batting beauty?
Just what you'd expect Hashim Amla to do. Sees it bowled short, so he just doesn't bother with it. That will be STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Short of a length delivery on middle and off, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Played back down the track by walking a step across. Was pitched on a length and Faf dealt with it well.
Length ball on middle and off, Amla moves inside the line, turns it on the on side with soft hands and scampers through for a single.
Cutting back in, blocked from within the crease.
Full ball outside off, du Plessis leans ahead and across to block it in front of point. Is off quickly and hence, has no problem in completing the run.
This will be the last over of the day...
Bowls it across the batsman, there is minimal bounce on this occasion. Hashim Amla leaves it alone as it goes on a few bounces to the keeper.
Short on middle and leg, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
Shortish in length outside off, Amla rises and punches it just wide of the man at cover, which allows him to take the run.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Bad signs for Bangladesh. Rahim is struggling with his leg. The skipper is really important to their cause. They will hope that it is nothing serious.

Amla crashes this through the covers and calls for the second. Both batsmen manage to do so as the throw comes in from the deep at the bowler's end. In the process, Rahim, who is backing up on this, gets hit on his shin and feels the sting. Bangladesh don't really want another one injured, do they?
Hits the deck hard and begins the over with a bumper. Amla keeps his eyes on the ball the whole time as he crouches low to let it sail over him.
Around off on a good length, defended well.
Good tap and run stuff from Hashim Amla. Pushes it in front of mid on and quickly sets off. Faf responds and both batsmen complete the run with ease.
Bouncer angling into the batsman, he pulls it along the ground to fine leg and gets one.
Full length delivery attacking the stumps, Faf brings down a straight blade in defense.
Length ball on off, Faf doesn't move at all as he blocks this comfortably down the track.
Stays rooted inside his crease and pushes this length ball back to the bowler.
Bumper to end the over, Hashim Amla ducks and evades. Wants nothing to do with that.
Banged in short again, Amla looks to fend it away but gets it off the glove, maybe the under edge of the top half of the bat behind. He's lucky the ball bounced over the stumps. Close call.
Some extra bounce as it's pitched on a length around off, tapped in front of cover from within the crease.
Short of a good length, angling across and there's some good bounce on it. Faf guides it square to point and runs across.
Just back of a length around off, du Plessis rises and punches it on the up, only to find mid off.
Length ball on leg stump line, whipped through square leg, to the man in the deep for a single.
Mustafizur Rahman to bowl again.
Tailing in, but it's going down leg. It's flicked down towards fine leg for a double.
Kicks off the deck a bit as Roy bowls it around off, du Plessis takes his bottom hand off as he defends it down on the off side.
Landed outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Short of a good length cutting back in this time, du Plessis with a beautiful straight bat defends it right back in the bowler's direction.
The second new ball has been taken. Will it bring a change in fortune for Bangladesh? Two slips in place.
Seaming away from a good length around off, Faf covers the line well and lets it be.
Good length delivery aimed at the top of off stump, du Plessis keeps bat and pad close together to guard it out.
Subashis Roy comes back for a burst.
FOUR! Just uses the pace of this well. Smartly done by Hashim Amla. Just tickles it off his pads and beats short fine leg. He tries to chase it down but the ball clearly wins the race.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Looped up outside off, Amla waits for the ball to drop and then drives it to the long off fielder. Single added to the scoreboard.
Pushes this into the covers, just a single taken.
Short and flat outside off, punched away off the back foot for no run.
Stays right behind the line and defends it out well.
FOUR! Quicker, flatter and outside off, Amla plays this very late and reaps dividends. Gets it off the outer half down towards third man for a boundary.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Wrists this fuller ball towards the man stationed at long on. One run to the total.
Coming into the batsman, he turns it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full again and outside off, driven through the cover area for another one.
Full and wide outside off, drilled hard through extra cover for a single. The 400 is up for the Proteas.
A walk across his sticks as Amla negotiates well. End of the over.

16th Test fifty for Faf du Plessis! He knocks it past the bowler, towards mid off and crosses over to the other end with all the time in the world. Gets to his milestone and it's been a good knock so far.
Faf has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.
Goes deep inside the crease, which allows him more time to play this. Worked away to square leg.
Full and flat, gets behind the line and blocks.
No spin for Sabbir, it's driven through mid off for a single.
Comes forward and defends with the full face of the bat.
Holding its line outside off, spanked into the gap on the off side for a couple.
Full ball is driven to mid off.
FOUR! Good shot. Has width offered to him, he takes it and sends it packing. Amla stays back and with a fierce cut through backward point sends it away to the boundary line.
Outside off, guarded off the back foot on the off side.
Sabbir Rahman to have a go with the ball.
Length ball around off, du Plessis looks to put bat on ball but gets an inside edge which just goes past the leg stump. Close call, could have easily gone on to knock the bails over.
Short again but this doesn't rise much. Du Plessis pulls it off the under edge to square leg.

Interesting conversation on-air. It is whether teams should get the pitches they want. The view for the opposition is that they should have all their bases covered so that they can adapt to the challenges. The consensus is that it should not be a problem for teams to get the pitches they want since it also presents different possibilities. The example cited is of India who had turners for teams with good fast bowlers and they had flat decks against England, who have a decent bowling attack.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shorter in length again, pulled away to fine leg to get off strike.
Shortish delivery on the stump, worked 'round the corner for an easy one.
Marginally ahead of a length just around off, Faf taps it down in front of covers.
The second new ball is available now. Remember, as per the new rules, reviews will not be refreshed.
Full in length, a tight defensive shot offered to keep it out.
Tossed up delivery around leg, Amla is down to play the paddle sweep but is caught on the pads. It is sliding down leg, hence no appeal.
FOUR! He's shifting gears here. Two in two for Hashim Amla. Full again and right in his slot, the maestro lofts it over mid off's head to send it across the rope.
FOUR! Sees the flight on this one and takes the aerial route. Dropped full, Amla smashes it over extra cover and finds the fence.
Full and straight, driven down the ground to long on for a single.
Straighter one outside off, Amla backs away and smacks it through covers for one.
Faf du Plessis has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Back of a length outside the line of off stump, Amla drops it in front of point and scurries across.

Short delivery angling back in on middle and leg, Amla pulls it with a lot of control as he places it towards fine leg. Runs the first one at a decent pace and still manages to come back for the second. Big gap out there, no trouble in doing so.
Serves it on a good length once more, Faf pierces the gap in the cover region and finds the sweeper. Gets a single to his name for doing so.
Short of a good length outside off, Hashim hangs back and punches it square through point for a single.
Just ahead of a length on the fifth stump line, knocked into the covers for nothing.

36th Test fifty for Hashim Amla! The maestro is piling on the runs again. Has looked comfortable since he's come on, pure class. He rocks back and crunches it through the gap in the covers for a single.
Full ball driven to mid off by Amla.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short in length again, du Plessis goes back, makes a little room and punches it to cover for one.
Full and straight from Mahmudullah, driven straight back to the bowler.
Dropped short on middle and off, punched off the back foot down to long on. Single taken comfortably.
Mahmudullah back on.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, Amla wrists it away on the leg side for a single.
Half-pulls this short ball in front of short mid-wicket, off the under edge for a brisk run. Played that late, hence didn't middle it.
Rock solid, is Faf du Plessis. He walks across a step to this length ball around off and offers a stylish defensive shot to short cover.
Short ball with no real venom in it, Amla rides the bounce as he pulls it along the ground through mid-wicket for a single.
Attempting to score the yorker, but fails and ends up bowling a low full toss. Faf comfortably flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Fraction straight in line, enough for Amla to lean across and whip it to deep mid-wicket. Single taken.
Rubel Hossain is back into the attack.
There are those fast hands again. Hashim stands tall and punches it through to sweeper cover. A run to end the over.
Another single. Down the ground to long on off the front foot.
Going on straight outside off, hit to the covers for one.
Sensible batting from the skipper. Just knocks it down to long on and brings Amla on strike.
FOUR! That's an excellent shot! Tossed up around off, du Plessis opens his body up a bit and drives it hard past mid off to send it across the rope.
Tad short, Amla stands tall and punches it back down the ground to long off for a single.
Full on leg, worked away on the on side for a run.
Quicker through the air on the stumps, blocked.

FOUR! Hashim Amla at his prolific best! He's a real treat to watch when he plays like that. Fuller ball outside off, he caresses the drive through the gap in the covers for a boundary. His fast hands do all the work, didn't require much footwork to put that away.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Again it's outside off, another leave by Amla.
Length delivery in the channel outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
The 350 is up for South Africa! Du Plessis drives it through wide mid off for a couple of runs.
No spin, no bounce and no drift as it's landed outside off, eased away to the covers for a single.
Some drift away from Hashim Amla, he reaches out to it and pushes it on the off side with soft hands.
Tossed up this time, knocked to long off for one.
Dropped on a length around off, it's punched solidly from within the crease to cover.
Flatter on middle, meets it with a solid, straight blade.
Speared full, tailing back in, catches Faf low on the pads as he misses his attempted flick shot. Runs down to fine leg and a leg bye is taken.
Short of a good length in line of the stumps, Amla with a little swivel pulls it behind square on the leg side to rotate strike.
Length delivery on the fourth stump line, blocked down in front of the cover area.
Amla with one of his whippy drives. Sees it outside off and looks to cash in, but is unfortunate to find the fielder.
On the pads, clipped to fine leg for an easy single.
Keeps it quite tight by bowling it close to off, pushed to the covers from within the crease.
Drifting in from around off, pushed just wide of mid off for a single.
Comes forward to this full ball and pushes it into the covers for one run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Some decent air on this, tossed right up there on middle and off, Amla opens his body up a bit and keeps it out on the off side.
Quicker again, Faf offers a firm back foot punch down to long on and crosses over.
Flatter, quicker and shorter on the stumps, du Plessis goes back and pushes it back down the track.
Drinks are on the field!
Full and outside off, driven to the left of the mid off fielder for a quick single.

Stifled appeal for a leg before, but it was always angling too far down. Fuller in length again, reverse on that. Catches Faf on the pads as he misses his flick. Sarkar pulls out of the appeal as soon as he begins it.
Faf du Plessis leans ahead to this fuller ball and clips it to the mid-wicket fielder in place.
Fullish length ball around the off stump line, defended.
Coming back in on a bit of a fuller length, Amla waits for the ball to come to him and works it on the leg side for a run.
Good yorker fired in on middle and leg, it's swinging back and threatening. But Faf is up to it as he digs it out towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full on middle and off, blocked presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR BYES! The 50-run stand is up with that. Darted down the leg side, Amla doesn't fiddle with it. Too hard for Liton Das behind the stumps to move to his left and collect that. It goes through him and away to the boundary line behind.
FOUR! A leg stump half-volley from Taijul, Amla with those beautiful wrists of his whips this hard through the right of mid on for a superb boundary.
Pushed quicker through the air, on off, Amla with a gentle push to the cover fielder.
Makes use of his feet, gets to the pitch and works it towards mid on again. Takes the fielder on this time and completes the run with ease. Good running.
Tossed up on middle stump, wristed down to mid on but it's straight to the fielder.
Nudged to fine leg from within the crease for an easy one.

FOUR! Another boundary for du Plessis! Wicket-to-wicket line from Sarkar, it's a bit too straight which is enough for the Protea skipper to take full advantage of. He flicks it through backward square leg and beats the man in the deep to the fence. Nicely done.
Fuller length ball, once again on off stump, a solid drive from Faf finds the man at mid off.
Length delivery on off, stays right behind the line and keeps it out safely.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, Faf picks it off his pads and works it behind square leg for a couple of runs.
Full and straight from Sarkar to start things off, du Plessis with a straight bat drives it straight back to him. The bowler sticks his right hand out and makes a good stop, saves runs.
Soumya Sarkar to bowl again.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Shortish around off, spinning away. Amla rocks back and cuts it behind point for a boundary.
Loopy delivery around off, Amla uses his feet and drives it to short mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Du Plessis plays it with soft hands to covers for a brisk single.
Landed around off again, played with the spin to covers.
Tossed up around off, eased to mid off.
Taijul Islam comes back for a bowl.
Another short ball on leg stump, pulled to backward square leg for a run.
FOUR! Du Plessis is getting used to the short stuff. He was looking a bit jittery but he is in the zone now. Bouncer in line of the stumps, pulled hard through mid-wicket for another boundary.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, drilled to covers.
FOUR! Well played! Banged halfway down the track on middle, du Plessis rides the bounce, gets on top of it and pulls it with authority through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Rahman rolls his fingers on this delivery and bowls it around off. Amla runs it down behind point for a run. Wants the second but du Plessis sends him back. Hashim has a wry smile on his face.
Angling away from Amla. He dabs it intentionally to the man at gully.
Fuller in length around off, du Plessis strides ahead and defends it calmly with a high elbow.
Back of a length outside off, Faf mistimes his punch to mid off.
FOUR! Shot! Short ball on middle and leg, du Plessis pulls it in a controlled manner through backward square leg to find the fence.
Length delivery outside off, shaping away this time. Faf makes a watchful leave.
Angling into Amla. Clipped through mid-wicket for a run.
In the zone outside off, left alone.

Dropped and FOUR! The short ball ploy almost did the trick again! Rahman hits the deck hard in line of the stumps. Du Plessis is drawn into the pull shot but is early into it. Ends up getting a top edge towards fine leg. Roy who is standing near the ropes charges towards the ball. It is dying on him as he dives full length but fails to take it. It goes right through his hands and through to the fence.
Good length delivery outside off, du Plessis is a little early into the drive. It goes uppishly towards mid off but falls well short of the fielder.
Similar length delivery around off, Faf du Plessis strides forward and pushes it to covers.
Fullish delivery outside off, Hashim strokes it to sweeper cover for a run.

FOUR! Easy pickings! That is the hallmark of a great player like him. He doesn't miss out on loose deliveries! Good length delivery around the hips, Amla hops and tucks it through backward square leg for a boundary. Timing at its best.
Fuller in length around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
In the corridor of uncertainty, du Plessis lets it go.
That's a peach! Faf almost fell prey to it. Good length delivery around off, seams away after hitting the deck. Du Plessis feels for it but is completely foxed by it.
Back of a length in the same channel, the Protea skipper stays back and plays it with an angled bat to point.
Fuller in length around off, tapped to covers.
Wide! Short delivery down the leg side, Faf moves inside the line and lets it go. Wide called for height.
On a length outside off, holding its line. Du Plessis plants his front foot across to allow it through.
Fuller length ball outside off, stays a touch low. Faf lets it go.
Well-directed bouncer around off, shoots through after landing. Amla does well to evade it.
Did you know? Before this innings, Bavuma went 10 successive innings where he managed double digits, this is his first single digit score since he scored 1 against NZ at Hamilton in 2017.
Rahman comes around the wicket now and bowls it on middle and leg, Faf clips it through backward square leg to rotate strike.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Things are happening now! Length delivery around middle, angling in a bit this time. Du Plessis is opened up in his stance as he looks to push it down the ground but gets an outside edge towards first slip. It falls short of the fielder and he fumbles. Two runs taken.
Straying on the pads, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller length delivery, slanting across Amla. He strides forward and blocks it right under his eyes.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
Good length delivery well outside off, du Plessis doesn't flirt with it.
Length delivery around off, swinging in. Faf covers the line and blocks it stoutly.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Good delivery to bowl first up to the skipper. Full length on off, angling in. Du Plessis does well to keep it out.
The skipper, Faf du Plessis comes out to bat.

OUT! Roy is on song! Intelligent bowling by him brings the reward. Good captaincy from Rahim too. He brought in two slips and a gully for this over. Subashis bowls this on a good length around off, gets it to seam away after pitching. There is a bit of extra bounce as well which unsettles Bavuma. He attempts to cut it through square of the wicket on the off side but only ends up getting a thick outside edge. Liton Das behind the stumps doesn't make a mistake this time around. Moves to his right to take a regulation catch. What a comeback from the visitors!
Length delivery outside off, Bavuma lets it go.
FOUR! Sweet! Amla plays that shot really well. Back of a length outside off, Hashim camps back and punches it with authority through covers for a boundary.
Sharp bumper around off, Hashim ducks under the bumper.
Half-volley outside off, Amla punches it on the up to covers where the fielder moves to his left to make a good stop.

Hossain changes his angle and runs in from around the wicket. Tries to tuck Bavuma but he is up for it. Plays it with soft hands to square leg and calls for a run immediately. Good judgement and the batsmen complete it with ease.
Wide! Short delivery outside off, takes off after landing. Bavuma ducks under it. Wide signaled for height.
Close! Back of a length outside off, shaping in substantially. Bavuma shapes for the cut but is cramped for room. Ends up chopping it just beside the stumps.

FOUR! That was asking to be hit and Bavuma obliges! Short and wide, Temba frees his arms and crashes it behind backward point for a rocketing boundary. Bangladesh were building good pressure. Can't afford to feed the new batsman loose deliveries.
On a length outside off, pushed off the back foot to covers for a brisk run.
Similar length delivery around off, good bounce on this occasion. Bavuma rides it and defends it beside the pitch on the off side.
Back of a length outside off, a bit of width on offer. Temba thinks about a cut but decides not to go for it.
Better from Roy! Brings this back in on a good length from outside off. Bavuma stands tall and taps it to point.
A bit wider this time, on a fullish length. Bavuma is not bothered to play at it.
In the corridor of uncertainty, holding its line. Temba doesn't fiddle with it.
Another sharp bumper on off, Amla has to sway away from the line of the delivery to evade it. Great stuff from Hossain. A productive over for SA comes to an end.
Fullish delivery, tailing in substantially. Bavuma clips it off the inner half to fine leg for a run to get off the mark.
Temba Bavuma strides out to bat.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Double bluff from Hossain does the trick! Markram is standing deep in the crease, expecting the short delivery. Instead, Rubel bowls a pinpoint yorker in line of the stumps. Aiden is caught in a tangle, with his feet going nowhere. Misses it completely and the middle stump goes for a toss. Brilliant passage of play for Bangladesh. Suddenly the energy levels are up and they are breathing fire at the moment! A terrific knock from the youngster comes to an end.
Hossain rolls his arms on this one, on a shorter length again. Pulled to square leg.

Timing and grace! Short of a length outside off, Amla punches it sweetly through covers. The fielder at sweeper cover has a lot of ground to cover to his right and does well. Saves a run for his side.
Hossain bends his back and hits the deck around off. Amla sits under the bumper quickly.

FOUR! Hit with power! Short delivery on middle and leg, comes at a nice height to Aiden. He swivels across and pulls it with aplomb through mid-wicket. Beats the diving fielder in the deep to pick up another boundary. 11 from the over.
Shortish outside off, pushed to wide mid off for a brisk single.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Fullish and straying on the pads, Amla clips it through mid-wicket to find the fence.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Back of a length outside off, punched through point fora run.

A better throw would have made things interesting! Good length outside off, Markram punches it through covers and calls fora couple. Mehedi (the substitute) races towards the ball and throws it towards the keeper's end. The throw is a bit wayward. Liton Das collects it and tries to flick it back on the stumps but fails. Close shave.
Subashis Roy to bowl from the other end.
Short stuff again around off, Hashim ducks under it.
Sharp movement on that occasion! Similar length outside off, jags back in. Amla hops and looks to push it to covers but gets an inside edge over the stumps. That was close.

FOUR! Shot! Back of a length outside off, Amla punches it crisply off his back foot through covers. Taijul Islam in the deep covers a lot of ground to his right, slides but seems to have failed to keep the ball in play. It is taken upstairs and the replays confirm it is a boundary.
Third bouncer in a row! Hossain runs in and hits the deck hard on middle, doesn't rise much after landing. Amla crouches, drops his wrists and leaves it uncomfortably.
Short again on middle and leg, pulled through mid-wicket for a run.
Begins with a shortish delivery on leg stump, as expected. Markram pulls it towards the fielder at backward square leg who dives to his right to make a good stop.

We are back for the final session. Aiden Markram and Hashim Amla to continue their innings. Can Bangladesh trigger a collapse? They will certainly strive for one. Rubel Hossain to begin first up with the ball after tea. A gully in place. Here we go...
...Day 1, Session 3...

The visitors need to bowl and field with more intensity if they are to create further inroads on a good batting surface. The hosts have continued to score freely putting away bad deliveries with ease. The spell from Rahman was a promising one and his teammates need to take a leaf out of it. Join us shortly for the evening session.

Another brilliant session for South Africa apart from the wicket of Dean Elgar at the fag end. Mustafizur Rahman was the one who used the short ball ploy to trouble the southpaw. He created an opportunity but it was not taken. However, Roy followed in his footsteps and made the plan work rather quickly.
Shorter in length around middle, Amla ducks under it. That's Tea, Day 1!
Fuller around off, Amla defends it watchfully.
Good length outside off, left alone.

NOT OUT! Close shave! Fuller in length around off, Amla comes forward to defend but gets hit on his pads. The bowler appeals long and hard but aborts after a point. Rahim comes over and has a chat with his bowler. He goes for the review. Replays show that Amla was fine as there was bat first and the Ball Tracker also shows that the impact is outside the line. Hence, Hashim survives. Bangladesh lose a review.
Another top edge! Markram top edges his pull again towards long leg for a single.
FOUR! No, no, no Taijul! Shorter in length around off, Markram pulls it through backward square leg. Taijul in the deep makes a meal of it and allows it through his legs for a boundary.

In the air...but safe! Suddenly the ball is in the air more than needed for the SA batsmen. Hossain bowls another bumper, Markram takes it on and looks to pull. The ball almost carries to the long leg fielder. A run taken. Nervy times before Tea.
Shorter in length around middle, pulled towards square leg.

TOP EDGED! Shorter in length around middle, Markram looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball flies down towards fine leg, Mominul slides near the fence and stops the ball. The umpire has a look since he is not sure. Replays find him safe and hence only two runs taken.
Length ball outside off, Amla taps it to covers and takes a single to get off the mark.
Good length outside off, Amla lets it go through watchfully.
Fuller outside off, driven to mid off for a single by Markram.
Rubel Hossain comes back on with Amla out to bat.
This one is pulled over mid-wicket off the toe end of the bat. Good running ensures that they get three.
Back of a length outside off, Markram dabs it towards short third man.
Hashim Amla walks in.

OUT! Elgar falls to the short ball and Mustafizur Rahman takes the catch. He is smiling since he knows that he set it up. Roy bowls a shorter one around leg, Elgar looks to pull it but gets a top edge and puts his head down as soon as he hits that. Rahman comes in from the deep at fine leg and takes a good tumbling catch. A wicket at last for the Tigers and it is a well-earned one. The marathon partnership comes to an end.
Similar shot, similar result. A run taken this time.
Shorter in length, sits up, Markram pulls it towards mid-wicket.

Yup, short is the order of the day! Banged in around middle, Elgar tucks it in front of backward square leg and wants a run. Aiden hesitates a touch but then goes through with the run. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end and hence, no harm done.
Subashis Roy returns for a bowl. Will he bowl short to Elgar as well?
Fuller around off, pushed towards mid off by the batsman.
Fuller around off, turned towards mid-wicket.
Aiden comes forward and defends it.
FOUR! What timing! Shorter in length outside off, Markram rocks back and punches it through cover-point. The sweeper cover cannot cut it off and the batsman gets a boundary.
Turns it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full toss outside off, punched towards deep mid on for a single.
Time for a change. Mominul Haque to bowl now.
Shorter in length around middle, Elgar ducks under it.
Angles across a good length ball outside off, Elgar drops his wrists and lets it go.
Similar length, Elgar pulls it towards short fine leg.

In the air but does not carry! Short again by Rahman, Elgar wants to pull it through but is late on the shot. The ball lobs on the bounce to mid on. Dean is starting to look a bit uncomfortable facing the short stuff.
Shorter in length around middle, Elgar ducks under it early.
Fuller in length around off, driven back to the bowler by Elgar. Rahman fumbles and parries it towards mid off but no harm done.
Stays back and punches it towards mid on from his crease.
FOUR! Whipped! Fuller on middle and leg, Markram takes a step forward and clips it hard between mid on and mid-wicket for a boundary.
Turns it towards backward square leg from his crease.
Fuller on middle and leg, driven towards the long off region. A single taken.
Punches one through mid on for a single.
FOUR! Hit away! Shorter in length around middle, Markram gets under it and pumps it over mid-wicket for a boundary.

DROPPED! Shorter in length from Rahman, Elgar once again gets into an awkward position as he looks to pull. The ball lobs off the gloves and goes behind. He was into the pull but was too late to play that shot. The keeper leaps to take the catch but can only lob it to his left. The first slip fielder tries to catch it but he too fails to do so. A chance, a real chance gone down. The visitors need to take their chances, maybe he could have timed his jump better.
Markram comes forward to defend but gets a edge through the vacant gully region for a single.
Fuller in length around off, Markram pushes it towards mid off lunging forward.
No ball! Sprays it outside off, Elgar pushes it towards covers for a quick single. He has overstepped and hence the umpire signals it a no ball. Replays show that the umpire got that one wrong.
Angles it around off, Elgar defends it towards mid on watchfully.
Good length outside off, placed towards covers from his crease.
Too full on middle and leg, dug out by Elgar from his crease.
Markram looks to go over mid on but mistimes it to the fielder.

NOT OUT! But well done, Das! Mahmudullah bowls it down the leg side, Markram fails to turn it through and the keeper whips the bails off in a flash and falls over. It is referred upstairs. Replays find Markram fine and hence he gets to bat on.
A stumping appeal against Markram has been referred upstairs. Great piece of glovework from Liton Das but the youngster is probably safe.
Floats it outside off, square driven towards point.
Darts it on a shorter length around middle and leg, Aiden cannot clip it away and is hit on his pads.
Flatter around off, Markram defends it from his crease.
Elgar works one through mid on for a single to rotate the strike.
Ouch! Shorter in length around leg, Elgar is happy to take it on his body and wears a blow on his shoulder. Markram calls him through for a leg bye.
Full and outside off, driven to the left of cover. The fielder parries it to the mid off fielder who then stops the ball from going through. A quick single.
Length ball around middle, Markram defends it from his crease.
Fuller on middle and leg, turned through square leg for a single.
Good length around off, Elgar defends it from his crease.
Fuller and outside off, Elgar drives it towards covers.
Bowling change, Mustafizur Rahman comes back on.
Fuller around off and middle, clipped to mid-wicket by Markram.
Flatter on middle and leg, turned through square leg for a single.

Stat Alert - The last time both openers scored tons in the same innings for SA in a Test was in 2008 - Neil McKenzie (138) and Graeme Smith (107) both scored tons in the same innings vs ENG at Lord's. Interestingly, this was after SA were made to follow-on.
Pushes this one towards mid off, the bowler goes to his right and stops the ball.
Fuller outside off, driven through wide mid off for a single.
Elgar drives it through the mid off region for a single.
Flatter around off, Elgar defends it from his crease.

FOUR! In the air.....but safe! A tad short outside off, Aiden wants to put it away and hence throws his bat at it. The ball bounces more and takes the edge. Thankfully for him, it flies over the slip cordon and runs into the third man fence for a boundary.
Good length ball wide outside off, another mistimed punch by Aiden.
Good length around off, Markram defends it from his crease.
Angles a good length ball around off, turned towards mid-wicket from his crease.
Length ball around off, Markram drives it back down the wicket. It is hit so straight that it hits the stumps at the other end.
Good length outside off, Markram mistimes his punch back down the wicket.
On middle and leg, Elgar turns it towards silly mid on. Two maidens in a row for Mahmudullah.
Quicker around off, Elgar presses forward and defends it.
Angles it around middle, Elgar comes forward and defends it.
Dean lunges forward and blocks this one watchfully.
Turns it towards square leg from his crease.
Too full on middle and leg, Elgar fails to clip it through. The keeper collects it well.
Good length around off and middle, Markram turns it towards the leg side.

FOUR! Mark that down, Aiden! Shorter in length, Markram is waiting for it and pulls it with disdain through backward square leg for a boundary. That is his maiden Test hundred, he will want to make this a big one, you don't get runs more easier than this. His teammates are delighted for him and why not! He's showing he could be the solution to South Africa's problems at the top.
FOUR! Sliced! Outside off on a length, Markram slices it behind point for a boundary. He moves to 97, his highest Test score.
Rahim is now holding his wrists. He dived on the previous ball to stop it. More trouble for the tourists.
Rubel bowls a full toss outside off, Elgar drives it towards the right of mid off. Rahim fumbles and allows a single.
Shorter in length around off, punched towards covers from his crease.
Good length around off, Elgar defends it from his crease.
Time for drinks!
Fires it on middle, turning back in. Markram flicks it to square leg.
Quicker but shorter in length on off. Markram whips it to mid on.
Works it with the spin to square leg.
Gives it air on off, Markram defends it towards covers.
Tosses it up on off, Aiden drives it back to the bowler.
Flatter on off, Aiden works it to mid-wicket.
Mahmudullah is into the attack.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Angles it down the leg side, the batsman misses the flick and it goes through to the keeper.
Back of a length on off, Aiden punches it through covers for a brace.
Just ahead of a length on off, Markram lunges forward and defends it towards mid off.
Good length on off, Markram defends it off the front foot.
Shorter in length outside off, Elgar guides it down to third man for a run.
Works it with the spin through square leg for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! 100 for Elgar! His 10th Test century! The man in form. A brilliant innings, he has been Bangladesh's nightmare. Islam serves him a half-volley outside off, too full in length so the spin is out of question. Elgar leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary. Back-to-back boundaries to bring up his ton.
FOUR! He moves onto 98! Islam bowls it flatter on off, turns back in. Elgar waits for the ball to do it's part and then flicks it fine through the leg side for a boundary.
Gives it a nice loop and lands it on off, Elgar drives it to mid off.
Plays it against the spin through square leg for a run.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Delightful! Roy serves a fuller delivery on off, Elgar leans into it and drives it through mid off for a boundary.
Fuller on the pads, Markram flicks it to fine leg for a run.
Angles it into the batsman. Elgar works it on the leg side for a run.
Markram's bat comes from an angle and he also pushes hard at the ball. Better bowling and late swing might trouble him.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Back of a length on off, Elgar guides it to point.
Just ahead of a length on off, Elgar defends it off the front foot.
Quicker on off, Markram defends it solidly.
Flatter on off, comes in with the arm. Aiden defends it off the front foot.
Full ball on off, Aiden drives it back to the bowler.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Floats it full on off, turning back in. Elgar flicks it through square leg for a couple.
Flatter on off, skids off the surface. Elgar tries to cut but gets a bottom edge and the ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Taijul Islam comes back into the attack.
Attacks the stump, hoping for Markram to fall over as he tries to flick. Aiden plays it with a straight bat to mid on.
Fuller outside off, Markram lets it be.
Lands it on a length on off, the batsman blocks it off the back foot.
Back of a length on off, Aiden punches it to covers.
FOUR! Runs are flowing here! Roy bowls it just short of a length on middle, Markram whips it through wide mid on. Mushfiqur gives it a chase but the ball wins as it crosses the fence.
Full and outside off, wanting the batsman to drive as he has a slip waiting. Markram resists the temptation and lets it through.
Comes around the wicket and bangs in a short one. Elgar does well to evade it.
FOUR! This time Fizz bowls it short which sits up to be hit as the wicket is a touch slow. Elgar rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Bowls it on a length on middle, stays a fraction low. Markram gets it off the toe end as he tries to flick towards mid-wicket for a run.
Shorter in length, not short enough to get the pull shot out. Elgar short arm jabs it through mid-wicket for three. Good running by the batsmen.
Some field changes. Backward square leg in place now while the deep square leg fielder moves finer.
Errs in line again, fails to build pressure. He bowls it on the pads. Aiden flicks it through the leg side for a run.
Full in length on off, Markram times it to covers.
Back of a length on off, Markram hops and punches it through point for a run.
Edged... but way short! Roy lands it on a length on off, stays a touch low. Markram tries to defend but gets an outside edge to gully.
Length ball on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Shorter in length, does not bounce enough. Markram shuffles across and clips it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Fuller in length on off, Dean eases it towards mid off for a run.

Another record - In 3 innings Markram and Elgar have put on 388 runs in 3 opening stands vs BAN this series. Combined, in 17 innings before this series this year, the total opening partnership runs was just 276.
Good length, pitches on middle and shapes away a touch. Elgar defends it.
Pace from both ends now! Subashish Roy is into the attack.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

OUCH! Kayes has been hit on the knee as he tried to stop the ball. He needs some medical attention, let us hope he is fine. He seems to be struggling and he is walking off the field. Mehedi Hasan is the substitute fielder in his place.

OUCH! That must have hurt! Good length on middle, jags away after pitching. Markram tries to defend but gets an outside edge which goes towards Kayes. He gets a bad bounce and gets hit on the knee as he tries stopping the ball. He looks in pain.
A good comeback delivery. Lands it on a length around off. Markram defends it off the back foot.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Markram! This is even better than the last one. Mustafizur bowls it full outside off, a half-volley. Aiden leans into it and drives it through covers. There was a sweeper in place but he had no chance. Top shot!
FOUR! He is dealing in boundaries here! Fuller in length by Rahman. Markram uppishly, drives it through covers and the ball races to the fence.
Shorter in length on leg stump, Elgar flicks it through square leg for a run.
FOUR! A poor ball to finish! Short and wide outside off, sits up to be hit. A hit-me ball actually. Markram cuts it through covers for a boundary.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Markram comes down the track, Islam sees him early and fires it outside off. Aiden adjusts and defends it.
Shorter in length on middle, Aiden punches it hard off the back foot towards the bowler. Islam makes a half-stop but no runs conceded.
Flatter on off, Markram defends it off the front foot.
Flicks it to mid-wicket with the angle.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.

FIVE WIDES! Mustafizur bangs in a short ball, he bends his back and gets it to skid off the surface. Elgar ducks under it and the ball beats the keeper and down to the fence. The umpire calls it a wide as the ball was way above the batsman's head.
Flicks it with the angle through mid-wicket for a run.
Around the wicket and lands it on a length on off, a effort ball by the Fizz. Markram defends it off the back foot.
Shorter in length outside off, Elgar guides it towards point to rotate strike.
Flicks it with the spin through square leg for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Drags his length back outside off, Markram pushes it through covers for a run.
FOUR! A gift but it still has to be put away! A full toss on middle, Markram with ease strokes it wide of mid off for a boundary.
Floats it full around off. The batsman eases it to mid off.
Did you know this? Elgar has only been dismissed once this year by a left-arm orthodox bowler.
Quicker on off, stays a touch low. Elgar off the back foot, places it towards cover-point for a run.
Rolls his fingers over the ball and bowls it outside off. The batsman opts not to fiddle with it.
Comes around the wicket and bowls a back of a length ball on off, Markram pushes it back to the bowler.
Good length outside off, Aiden lets it be.
FOUR! Errs in line and bowls it full on the pads, Markram is too good a player to miss out on those. He flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Very simple!
Short and wide, hit straight to the sweeper at point for a single.
A good start by Rahman. He lands it on a length on middle, angling away. Aiden guides it to deep point for a run.
Mustafizur Rahman will bowl from the other end. He has a slip and a gully in place.
Drags his length back on off, Aiden camps back and punches it through covers for a run.
Clips it with the spin through square leg for a run.
Gives it air on off, too full but. Elgar drives it to mid off.
Flatter on off, turning back in. Elgar with the spin works it to square leg.
A high full toss, it may have slipped out of his hand. Markram flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. Islam is lucky he got away with that.
Starts off with a loopy delivery on off, Markram defends it off the front foot.
So, we are back after the delay and all set to get underway. Taijul Islam will continue his bowling. Markram is on strike to face him and Elgar is at the other end.

We're all set to get underway after the break. The men who matter are out in the middle. Dean Elgar and Aiden Markram will resume their innings. But hold on... It seems we are going to have a 10-minute delay as the food for the Bangladesh team arrived late. That's a first!
...Day 1, Session 2...

Both Elgar and Markram have scored fifties and should be eyeing huge scores since only they can get themselves out. The Tigers are being tamed like cats away from home. If they don't take an early wicket, it could be a long, long day for them. Wickets are the order of the day for them. The Saffas will aim to bat long, big and once. Join us in a while for the second session.

Brilliant session for South Africa! Bangladesh won the toss and did the hosts a favour by handing them the advantage of being able to bat first on this batting beauty. The grass before the game may have taken the tourists for a ride. There is no grass and there seemed to be no plans by the away side. They have been all over the place, unable to create any kind of pressure.
Good length on off, angling away. He defends it off the back foot and starts walking towards the dressing room. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under it.
Just behind a length on off, Markram taps it towards cover-point for a quick run. They are rotating strike so easily.
Full in length outside off, inviting the batsman to drive. He resists and lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length outside off, Markram guides it wide of deep point for two.
Back of a length outside off, Elgar pushes it through cover-point for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Quicker on off, Aiden defends it solidly.

FOUR! Fifty for Markram. The youngster brings up his second in as many matches. He too is continuing from where he left. This time he would want to make it big. He uses his feet to get to the pitch of the ball and flicks it through the gap between mid-wicket and mid on for another boundary.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full toss, drives it hard to the man at short mid off.

FOUR! What a shot! Just shows how good a surface this is. Top, top wrist work. Islam goes wide of the crease and bowls a flatter delivery but shorter in length on middle. Markram rocks back and whips it through mid on for a boundary.
Back of a length on middle, Dean flicks it to mid-wicket.
Waste of effort from Rubel. He comes running in, bangs in a short ball but down the leg side. Elgar  evades it.
Bouncer! Elgar ducks under it.
FOUR! This is too easy for Elgar! They are providing him freebies. A half-volley outside off. Elgar times it through covers and into the fence.
Good length on off, Elgar defends it to mid off.
Shortish in length outside off, Markram cuts it through cover-point. There is protection in the so only a single conceded.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! A gift but still has to be put away! A similar length to the last delivery but this time a but wider. Elgar cashes in on the width and drives it crisply through covers for a boundary.
Fuller and outside off, Elgar drives it straight to the man at covers.
Floats it outside off, turning back in. Elgar shuffles across and works it on the leg side.
Flatter from over the wicket on off, Elgar with the spin works it towards mid-wicket.
Loopy ball on middle, very full so the spin is out of question. Markram drives it hard past the bowler and down to long off for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Milestone alert - This is the fourth century stand by an opening pair for SA against BAN in Tests. Highest: 415 by McKenzie/G Smith at Chittagong, 2008.
Shorter in length outside off, Aiden cuts it but not off the middle towards cover-point for a run.
Lands it on a length, nips into the batsman a touch after pitching. Aiden flicks it to mid-wicket.
A better length, fullish around off. Elgar guides it down to deep point for a run.
Shortish ball outside off, Elgar guides it to point.
FOUR! Bad ball and dispatched to the boundary! Rubel starts off with a loosener outside off, short and width on offer. Elgar has plenty of time to get back and push it through covers for a boundary.
Rubel Hossain is back into the attack.
Gives it a nice loop on off, Markram mistimes his drive back to the bowler.
Fires it on off, Markram defends it off the front foot.
Drags his length back outside off, Elgar punches it against the spin through covers for a run.
Shorter in length on off, Elgar shuffles across and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Floats it full on middle, Elgar pushes it back to the bowler.
Flatter outside off, goes on with the angle. Elgar guides it down through short third man and some good running from the batsmen help them to take two.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Classy! Roy bowls it shorter in length around off, Markram has all the time in the world as he rocks back and punches it through covers for a boundary.
Short and on leg stump. Too easy for Elgar as he clips it around the corner for a run.
Good length on off, Markram taps it towards point and sets off for a run. The fielder is quick to the ball and hits bull's eye at the non-striker's end but the batsman has made his ground.
Angles it into the batsman, Aiden plays it to mid on.
Shorter in length around leg stump. Elgar works it towards square leg with soft hands for a run.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Plays it with the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
Drags his length back on middle, Markram punches it towards mid on for a run.

FOUR! Excellent use of the feet from the youngster! Islam gives it air on middle. Markram comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Easy for South Africa here.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy ball on middle, Markram drives it back to the bowler.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Bouncer, trying to surprise the batsman. Elgar evades it quite comfortably.
Full again on off, looking for an edge. Elgar drives it back to Roy who bends down and makes a good stop.
Good length on off, Elgar defends it off the front foot.
Fuller in length again on off, Elgar eases it to mid off.

FOUR! Fifty for Elgar! His 9th in Tests. He has continued from where he left off in the first game. What timing! Beautiful! Roy changes the angle and comes around the wicket, lands it outside off on a length. Elgar punches it through the covers on the up for a boundary. That was extremely pleasing to the eye.
Floats it full on off, Aiden drives it back to the short mid off fielder who scores a direct hit at the striker's end but no harm done.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
An arm ball on middle, Markram lunges forward and defends it.
Drags his length back, around off. Elgar camps back and punches it past the diving bowler and down to long on for a run.
Floats it around off, Elgar defends it.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Islam tosses it up outside off, offers width to Elgar. He leans into it and drives it through the gap between covers and mid off for a boundary.
FOUR! Too easy! Roy tries to bowl a bouncer but without a lot of fizz! It sits up to be hit, Markram pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary.
Again hits the length around off, Markram with relative ease defends it.
Fuller in length on middle, Elgar shuffles across and times it towards mid on for a quick single.
Shortish in length, not very short. Markram picks the length early and pulls it towards deep square leg for a run.
Good length on off, around the off stump, looking for an edge. Markram camps back and defends it back to the bowler.
Roy comes running in and lands it on a length outside off. There is no swing on offer. The batsman covers the line and defends it.
Quicker on off, goes on with the arm. Elgar prods forward and blocks it.
Tosses it up, very full but down the leg side. Markram again flicks it fine past the short fine leg fielder. Rahman there gives it a chase and saves a run for his team. Good running by the batsmen.
Floats it up on off, the batsman defends it solidly.
Fires it on the pads. Too easy for Markram who flicks it fine down the leg side for a couple.
Works it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Flatter on off, Markram defends it off the front foot.

CLOSE SHAVE! That came back in sharply! Roy lands it on a length outside off, gets it to jag back in sharply. Elgar watchfully leaves it but it was very close to the off pole. A brave leave in the end.
Bangs in a short one which bounces way above the batsman's head. Elgar watches it early and ducks under it.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batsman. Markram flicks it with the angle through square leg for a run.
Shortish length around off, Markram punches it to the man at covers.
Back of a length on off, angling into the batsman. Markram defends it off the back foot.
Shorter in length, comes slow off the wicket. Elgar rocks onto the back foot and works it towards square leg for an easy run.
Darts it on off, Markram lunges forward in defense.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Islam tosses it up on middle, but it is very full. Markram moves his front leg out of the way and hits it uppishly towards mid on. There are shouts of catch it but there is no one there. The ball races to the fence.
Fires it on middle, Markram defends it solidly.
Full toss, a gift on middle. Markram drives it straight back to the bowler. He will be dissapointed he did not put that away.
Flatter on off, goes on with the arm. Markram prods forward in defense.
Time for some spin! Taijul Islam is into the attack.
Bangs in a surprise bouncer on leg. Elgar ducks under it.
Just ahead of a length on middle, Elgar drives it back towards the bowler who crouches down in his followthrough and makes a half-stop.
Fuller in length this time around off, angling away from the batsman. Elgar with a lot of ease defends it.
Roy pitches it on a length on middle. Markram tucks it with soft hands towards mid on for a run.
Lands it on a length around off, Markram, off the back foot defends it onto the ground.
Starts off with a fuller length delivery outside off, no swing on offer. Markram watchfully leaves it.
Subashis Roy is back on.

Drinks! A harmless first hour for the hosts as the tourists are making the same mistakes again. They chose to bowl first but are hardly bowling troubling lines and lengths. Rahim can continue to complain, as they wait for a wicket.

OUCH! Shorter in length from Rahman from round the wicket, Elgar takes his eyes off that one and just fends at it. The ball lobs off the arm and flies towards the keeper. Liton moves to his right and catches it. There is a slight appeal but the umpire stays put as he had spotted that there was no bat there.
Shorter in length outside off, punched towards point from his crease.
Bouncer! Shorter in length outside off, Elgar ducks under it.
Shorter in length outside off, Elgar defends it watchfully.
FOUR! Another boundary! Shorter in length outside off, Elgar punches it through backward point. The fielder cannot cut it off inside the 30-yard region and Dean gets a boundary.
Good length around middle, Elgar tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Outside off on a length, defended watchfully.

Fuller in length outside off, Elgar drives it on the up to the left of mid off. Rahman gives a chase and keeps the ball in play. Three runs taken, 50 up for South Africa. Back-to-back 50-run stand for the SA openers.
Elgar comes forward and defends it.
FOUR! Runs keep flowing! Shorter in length, Elgar picks it early and pulls it through the mid-wicket region for a boundary. This is nothing bowling by the tourists. 7th boundary for Elgar already!
Shorter in length around leg, Elgar ducks under it from his crease.
Good length outside off, Elgar comes forward and pushes it through covers for a couple of runs.
Shorter in length around middle, Markram taps it towards short leg with a little hop.
BEATEN! Angles it around off, Markram pushes at it from his crease. The ball holds its line and beats the outside edge. Bangladesh have bowled far too few of these.
Shorter in length outside off, Aiden rides the bounce and taps it towards gully.
Full and outside off, Markram lets it go through watchfully.
A bit of a halt. There is some movement behind the sightscreen.
Shorter in length outside off, Elgar pulls it over mid-wicket for a single.
Good length around off, Elgar defends it.
